name: Rice
how_it_helps_soil: Its roots and leftover straw may add organic material when managed locally.

name: Wheat
how_it_helps_soil: Leaving suitable crop residues may help protect the soil surface.

name: Rabi jowar (sorghum)
how_it_helps_soil: Its deeper roots may help open channels in the soil.

name: Bajra (pearl millet)
how_it_helps_soil: Keeping its residues on the field may help cover the soil.

name: Maize
how_it_helps_soil: Its residues may return organic material to the soil.

name: Soybean
how_it_helps_soil: With suitable soil microbes, its roots may add nitrogen to the soil.

name: Groundnut
how_it_helps_soil: With suitable soil microbes, it may add nitrogen for a later crop.

name: Chickpea (chana)
how_it_helps_soil: With suitable soil microbes, it may add nitrogen to the soil.

name: Tur (pigeon pea)
how_it_helps_soil: Its deeper roots and nitrogen-fixing partners may help the next crop.

name: Moong (mung bean)
how_it_helps_soil: A short crop may cover otherwise bare soil and add nitrogen with suitable microbes.

name: Cotton
how_it_helps_soil: Its deep roots may leave channels after harvest, depending on soil management.

name: Fodder sorghum
how_it_helps_soil: Its roots and remaining cover may help reduce exposed soil.

name: Indian mustard (sarson)
how_it_helps_soil: A different plant family may interrupt some cereal-linked pest cycles; local pests and residue management still need review.
